simple.meaning: בָּלַק (bâlaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to annihilate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Isaiah, Nahum, beginning at Isaiah 24:1. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּלַק (H1110) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּלַק (bâlaq) / H1110 is traced through Isaiah 24:1, Nahum 2:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1110. balaq [ בָּלַק ] verb waste, lay waste (Assyrian balâ‡u , Pi`el destroy , Lyon Sargon 61 ; compare Arabic a desert ) — Po`el Participle without מ , suffix בּוֺלְקָהּ Isa 24:1 (|| בּוֺקֵק , subject ׳י , object הארץ ); — on form (which might also be Qal Participle) compare Ol § 254 Lag GN 1882, 403 ; also בקק Po. Jer 51:2 , and intensive use of Infinitive absolute Niph`al Isa 24:3 ; further Punic (i.e. intensive) Participle Nahum 2:11 (this however perhaps largely influenced by assonance). Pu`al Participle מְבֻלָּקָ֑ה Nahum 2:11 ( ומב וּמְבוּקָה ׳בּוּקָה ), devastated , or as substantive a devastated city.
